title: United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week — 2026
bluf: General Debate Day One closed with thirty-one scheduled national addresses plus Argentina's right of reply; speeches added political and institutional signals, not negotiated outcomes. The Workbench preserves both the 19:34 in-progress snapshot and a final-session official-caption source with 36,712 raw cues de-rolled into 8,985 windows. A late-release sweep now preserves 23 speaker-authorized statement PDFs: twenty newly posted files totaling 202 visually inspected pages, three previously held, and eight country pages still without a PDF at cutoff. Those eight no-PDF pages later exposed UN-published English AI transcript downloads, all now preserved; token comparison proves they are country clips of the same UN caption family rather than independent transcript passes. Every country receives a compact primary-source summary; Brazil, the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom, Croatia, Morocco and now Bhutan cross the deep-audit threshold, while Belgium, Kyrgyzstan, Korea and Naoero receive targeted institutional-object treatment. Bhutan's Royal Charter and enacted law confirm the GMC authority shell, but digital-currency, 25-GW date, nearly $5 billion negotiation and construction claims remain separate clocks. The September 23 preflight freezes thirty-seven scheduled—not delivered—national interventions and separates them from the concurrent Right to Development plenary and climate leaders event. The development meeting's separate public list has 127 approved inscriptions, all still not ready and not done, plus one non-approved raw slot absent from the rendered list. Its permitted speaking time would require 389 minutes against only 310 programmed plenary minutes, proving the list is a demand queue rather than a plausible delivered roster; twenty-one countries also appear on the General Debate roster, but only four list the same planned representative in both streams. The legal-process baseline further separates the adopted non-treaty 1986 Declaration, operating Working Group/Special Rapporteur/Expert Mechanism/OHCHR machinery and still-draft covenant. The HRC transmitted that draft by 29–13–5; the 2025 Working Group retained divergent views; HRC resolution 60/7 continued the machinery by 28–14–5; and A/RES/80/207, adopted 127–23–32, records a political impasse and authorizes today's commemoration without adopting the covenant. Eight governing UN PDFs totaling 121 visually inspected pages now anchor the speech receipt ladder. The four official Day Two WebTV event objects are locked as capture routes, but pre-publication remains distinct from a held event or delivered statement. A reusable official-source capture tool has been proved against Day One and all four Day Two before-states remain lower-state objects. At 00:21 EDT, all thirty-seven Day Two schedule cards were published but none exposed a country-page link. The 20:45 UTC UN Journal issue now assigns distinct UUIDs to the 7th and 8th plenary meetings and to both Right to Development sessions. The two General Debate records share one WebTV entry, the development records use separate entries, and all four official eStatements containers remain empty. This advances meeting identity and publication apparatus, not delivery. At 01:47 EDT, a second official Right to Development speaker-list capture moved Costa Rica from slot 36 to 98 and changed the planned representative from the foreign minister to the vice minister for multilateral affairs; sixty-two intervening entries shifted one slot while the 127-approved and zero-ready/done/skip totals stayed fixed. The original and revised versions are both preserved. No controlling finding depends on media indexing. Event, prepared speech, delivery, interpretation, caption, claim, authorization, funding, treaty adoption, entry into force, deployment, operation and legal settlement remain separate clocks. At 02:17 EDT, the preserved official General Debate raw feed confirms the same thirty-seven approved public-roster speakers plus two unapproved afternoon records—Italy and Uzbekistan—with no ready/done/skip/end-time advance. A same-window checksum return found all twenty-three Day One formal PDFs unchanged, and the 02:12 comparison found all four Day Two WebTV objects unchanged. At 02:32 EDT, the reusable official Journal API comparator found all four records still open and unchanged at zero attached statements, documents and summaries. The Day One compact-versus-escalated practice is now a reusable validated register contract: all delivered addresses must be summarized, temporary omissions must be explicit and targeted/deep treatment requires a material reason. At 03:28 EDT, a five-surface return found the roster byte-identical, all four WebTV objects unchanged, all four Journal records still empty/open, the Syria shell asset-empty and all 37 schedule cards still unlinked. At 04:52 EDT, the explicitly selected Day Two schedule remained at zero links, Syria remained asset-empty and the home-page speaking/closed/previous chrome still described Day One; stale page furniture does not establish Day Two delivery. The 05:13 Syria deep-review baseline now separates eight authority, sanctions, control and execution clocks and preserves 35 visually inspected pages, so Al-Sharaa's eventual speech can be tested against controller-specific receipts rather than treating recognition, sanctions relief, integration or reconstruction as single events. At 05:40 EDT, the Iran baseline corrected the earlier no-agreement wording: a signed 17 June Islamabad interim memorandum exists, but its 60-day final-deal and implementation sequence did not mature. Three formal UN PDFs totaling 25 inspected pages now separate safeguards law, actual IAEA knowledge, JCPOA commitments, the Secretariat's restored-sanctions operation, the China-Russia-Iran legal objection, active U.S. pressure and the force/ceasefire/maritime clock. Trump's isolation request and deal forecast are the coercive and incentive sides of an unresolved strategy, so Iran is presumptively deep after delivery. At 06:00 EDT, the roster, four WebTV objects and four Journal records remained unchanged. The 06:04 Argentina baseline adds four UN PDFs totaling 21 inspected pages and distinguishes title, UN recommendations, competing legal theories, negotiation, administration, resource operation, domestic enforcement and foreign commercial effect. Decree 868/2026 joins Foreign Ministry enforcement to RIGI investment and hydrocarbon-permit screens; the announced 60 subjects remain proceedings rather than final sanctions or convictions. Argentina is presumptively deep only if the delivered address moves one of those clocks. At 07:04 EDT, the Workbench transcript from the official White House Trump–Zelenskyy bilateral recording narrowed Patriot production to possible and under discussion, H.R. 5334 to enacted authority under study, and the Iran development to a U.S.-characterized three-hour meeting and intended follow-up without Iranian confirmation, terms or implementation.

Preserve the evidence cutoff. Verify time-sensitive claims with fresh primary sources.
Use public_reading materials directly. Treat private_library_metadata entries as existence and routing signals only.
Keep fact, project inference, strongest rival, unresolved object and falsifier separate.
